readout_other: Open-field behavior (movement time/speed, head scratching, grooming); intrinsic signal optical imaging (ISOI) of cortical deoxyhemoglobin (HbR); single-channel LFP power spectra; plasma CGRP ELISA; cortical CGRP and c-Fos Western blot
direction_notes: TUS decreased the NTG-elevated 0.5-4 Hz LFP power band while increasing the NTG-suppressed 4-40 Hz power bands, returning both toward control levels; TUS also kept cortical HbR close to control levels (inhibiting the NTG-induced decrease) and reduced NTG-elevated plasma CGRP, cortical CGRP, and cortical c-Fos.

exposures.label: Cortical TUS at NTG injection / imaging window

target.label: cerebral cortex beneath the cranial imaging window (2 mm posterior, 2 mm lateral to bregma)

flags.reason: Group sizes (Ctrl+TUS n=6, NTG+TUS n=9) are reused across separate behavioral, optical imaging, and LFP recording sub-experiments using different groups of mice, and a separate n=7 is used for biochemical analysis; the total unique number of TUS-exposed animals is not stated (total across the whole study is 127 mice for all purposes).

The stimulation site is described only by stereotaxic coordinates relative to bregma ('the image window', -2 mm AP, 2 mm ML), without naming a specific cortical subregion; recorded as generic cerebral cortex.

Pulse duration (50 ms) is derived from the number of cycles per pulse (NC=25000) divided by the fundamental frequency (500 kHz), consistent with duty cycle (5%) / PRF (1 Hz); this conversion is explicitly sanctioned by the extraction instructions.

Surgery for window/electrode implantation was performed under isoflurane anaesthesia, but the paper does not explicitly state whether animals were awake or anaesthetised during the TUS/behavioral/LFP recording sessions themselves; 'awake' is inferred from the freely-moving LFP recording and open-field behavioral testing.
